newsitem.title: USA: Edison 1,070 MW nuke moves to hot standby.
newsitem.headline: Edison 1,070 MW nuke moves to hot standby.

text.p: Southern California Edison Co's 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre nuclear power unit 2 had moved to a hot standby mode as of early Monday in preparation for a restart from a maintenance outage, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The unit was in "mode 3 - hot standby" and was set to restart on Monday, the NRC said in its daily plant status report for Monday.
The unit had been in a cold shutdown mode as of late last week.
A company spokesman has said the unit was expected to remain shut until March 20.
The unit, located in San Clemente, Calif., was taken off line Nov 30 for scheduled refueling and maintenance.
An expected resumption of operations at the unit was postponed for further repairs.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 3 was operating at full power as of early Monday, the NRC said.
The San Onofre plant is majority owned by Edison, while Enova Corp subsidiary San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own the remaining five percent.
